scenes.tts: What happens when something holds hemoglobin in the wrong shape, or makes one shape dangerous?
scenes.visual: Title fades. Two warning icons: a CO molecule and a crescent-shaped red cell. On screen: When the shapes betray you.
scenes.narration: What happens when something holds hemoglobin in the wrong shape, or makes one shape dangerous?

scenes.tts: Carbon monoxide binds the heme about two hundred fifty times more tightly than oxygen does.
scenes.caption: Carbon monoxide (CO) binds the heme about 250 times more tightly than oxygen does.
scenes.visual: CO binding straight on to one heme. On screen: about 250-fold tighter than O₂.
scenes.narration: Carbon monoxide (CO) binds the heme about 250 times more tightly than oxygen does.

scenes.tts: Like oxygen, it favors R. So it shifts the mix toward R.
scenes.visual: The population bar tips toward R as CO binds.
scenes.narration: Like oxygen, it favors R. So it shifts the mix toward R.

scenes.tts: Predict. One subunit carries carbon monoxide. Is the oxygen on the other three held more or less tightly?
scenes.visual: A tetramer with CO on one heme and O₂ on the other three. Question on screen: more or less tightly held?
scenes.narration: Predict. One subunit carries carbon monoxide. Is the oxygen on the other three held more or less tightly?

scenes.tts: More tightly. The molecule is held in R, so its oxygen is released far less readily. The curve shifts left.
scenes.visual: The three O₂ stay aboard as the cell passes muscle. The curve slides left.
scenes.narration: More tightly. The molecule is held in R, so its oxygen is released far less readily. The curve shifts left.

scenes.tts: So carbon monoxide takes sites away from oxygen, and it makes the oxygen still aboard stay put.
scenes.visual: Two labels: one site lost to CO; the remaining O₂ held tighter.
scenes.narration: So carbon monoxide takes sites away from oxygen, and it makes the oxygen still aboard stay put.

scenes.tts: Carbon monoxide hemoglobin is bright red. But the classic cherry-red skin is rarely seen in living patients.
scenes.visual: A vial of bright red blood. Label: cherry-red skin rarely seen in living patients.
scenes.narration: Carbon monoxide hemoglobin is bright red. But the classic cherry-red skin is rarely seen in living patients.

scenes.tts: A pulse oximeter cannot tell it from oxygen hemoglobin. It reads falsely normal while tissues suffocate.
scenes.visual: A fingertip pulse oximeter showing a normal reading; muscle cells beside it dimming.
scenes.narration: A pulse oximeter cannot tell it from oxygen hemoglobin. It reads falsely normal while tissues suffocate.

scenes.tts: The fix is high-concentration oxygen, to compete the carbon monoxide back off.
scenes.visual: Oxygen mask; O₂ dots displace CO from the heme.
scenes.narration: The fix is high-concentration oxygen, to compete the carbon monoxide back off.

scenes.tts: Sickle-cell disease is a different failure. Here the T shape itself turns sticky.
scenes.visual: A deoxy (T) hemoglobin molecule with a sticky spot glowing on its surface.
scenes.narration: Sickle-cell disease is a different failure. Here the T shape itself turns sticky.

scenes.tts: One amino acid changes. Glutamate becomes valine at position six of the beta chain.
scenes.caption: One amino acid changes. Glutamate becomes valine at position 6 of the β chain.
scenes.visual: Sequence strip: β chain position 6, Glu → Val.
scenes.narration: One amino acid changes. Glutamate becomes valine at position 6 of the β chain.

scenes.tts: That valine sits on the surface in every state. But in T, a neighbor's hydrophobic pocket opens, and the valine plugs in.
scenes.visual: Val6 on the surface of one HbS molecule in both shapes. On a deoxy (T) neighbor a pocket (Phe85, Leu88) opens, and the valine docks into it.
scenes.narration: That valine sits on the surface in every state. But in T, a neighbor's hydrophobic pocket opens, and the valine plugs in.

scenes.tts: That neighbor sticks to the next. The molecules polymerize into stiff fibers that deform the red cell into a crescent.
scenes.visual: Molecules join into long fibers; a disc-shaped red cell bends into a crescent.
scenes.narration: That neighbor sticks to the next. The molecules polymerize into stiff fibers that deform the red cell into a crescent.

scenes.tts: So the trigger is losing oxygen. Exertion raises oxygen use. Cold slows blood through small vessels.
scenes.visual: Two icons: a runner (more O₂ use) and a snowflake (slower flow in small vessels).
scenes.narration: So the trigger is losing oxygen. Exertion raises oxygen use. Cold slows blood through small vessels.

scenes.tts: Both leave more hemoglobin in T for longer. Dehydration concentrates sickle hemoglobin, so fibers form faster.
scenes.visual: Population bar held toward T; a shrinking water drop beside denser HbS molecules.
scenes.narration: Both leave more hemoglobin in T for longer. Dehydration concentrates sickle hemoglobin, so fibers form faster.

scenes.tts: Carriers with one copy are usually healthy. They are partly protected against severe falciparum malaria.
scenes.visual: One normal and one sickle gene copy. Label: usually healthy; partly protected against severe falciparum malaria.
scenes.narration: Carriers with one copy are usually healthy. They are partly protected against severe falciparum malaria.

scenes.tts: One newer treatment uses gene editing to switch fetal hemoglobin back on.
scenes.visual: Gene-editing scissors at a switch labelled BCL11A enhancer; fetal γ-globin turns on.
scenes.narration: One newer treatment uses gene editing to switch fetal hemoglobin back on.

scenes.tts: Fetal hemoglobin does not join the sickle polymer. It dilutes the sickle hemoglobin around it, so cells sickle far less.
scenes.visual: Fetal hemoglobin molecules scattered among HbS; fibers break up; cells stay round.
scenes.narration: Fetal hemoglobin does not join the sickle polymer. It dilutes the sickle hemoglobin around it, so cells sickle far less.

scenes.tts: Almost everything in this story follows one rule. Hemoglobin is a mix of a weak shape and a tight shape.
scenes.visual: Recap strip: T and R, with oxygen, BPG, acid, CO₂, CO and fetal hemoglobin each placed on the side it favors.
scenes.narration: Almost everything in this story follows one rule. Hemoglobin is a mix of a weak shape and a tight shape.

scenes.tts: Oxygen shifting that mix is how blood delivers. Locking the mix, or making T sticky, is how it fails.
scenes.visual: End card. LINE: Oxygen shifting the T and R mix delivers; locking it, or a sticky T, causes disease.
scenes.narration: Oxygen shifting that mix is how blood delivers. Locking the mix, or making T sticky, is how it fails.

scenes.visual: End card. LINE: Oxygen shifting the T and R mix delivers; locking it, or a sticky T, causes disease.
